messages.subject: Multilevel model with two groups
parts:
Hi all, 

I'm trying to estimate a multilevel model where I have 2 groups present in the data set. I want to estimate what is essentially the same model in both groups - however, the items that are used to assess each variable are different for each group, but the constructs are the same. I am primarily interested at what is happening at level 1 (within-person level, we gave the participants the same surveys for 10 days, each person got a morning, afternoon, and evening survey on each day). Theoretically the same relationships could hold both within people and between people. I've taken a few different approaches.

First, I estimated the model I'm interested in at level 1, and a saturated model at level 2 (same for both groups). Here is that syntax:

multilevel.multigroup.regression.model.revised <- ' 
group: 1
level: 1 
s1_dv1 ~ a1*s1_iv1 + a2*s1_iv2 + a3*s1_med1 + a4*s1_med2 + a5*s1_med3 + a6*s1_med4
s1_dv2 ~ b1*s1_iv1 + b2*s1_iv2 + b3*s1_med1 + b4*s1_med2 + b5*s1_med3 + b6*s1_med4

#s1_med1 ~ e1*s1_iv1 + e2*s1_iv2
#s1_med2 ~ f1*s1_iv1 + f2*s1_iv2
#s1_med3 ~ g1*s1_iv1 + g2*s1_iv2
#s1_med4 ~ h1*s1_iv1 + h2*s1_iv2

level: 2 
s1_dv1 ~~ s1_iv1 + s1_iv2 + s1_med1 + s1_med2 + s1_med3 + s1_med4 + s1_dv2
s1_dv2 ~~ s1_iv1 + s1_iv2 + s1_med1 + s1_med2 + s1_med3 + s1_med4
s1_iv1 ~~ s1_iv2 + s1_med1 + s1_med2 + s1_med3 + s1_med4
s1_iv2 ~~ s1_med1 + s1_med2 + s1_med3 + s1_med4
s1_med1 ~~ s1_med2 + s1_med3 + s1_med4
s1_med2 ~~ s1_med3 + s1_med4
s1_med3 ~~ s1_med4


group: 2
level: 1 

s2_dv1 ~ c1*s2_iv1 + c2*s2_iv2 + c3*s2_med1 + c4*s2_med2 + c5*s2_med3 + c6*s2_med4
s2_dv2 ~ d1*s2_iv1 + d2*s2_iv2 + d3*s2_med1 + d4*s2_med2 + d5*s2_med3 + d6*s2_med4

#s2_med1 ~ i1*s2_iv1 + i2*s2_iv2
#s2_med2 ~ j1*s2_iv1 + j2*s2_iv2
#s2_med3 ~ k1*s2_iv1 + k2*s2_iv2
#s2_med4 ~ l1*s2_iv1 + l2*s2_iv2

level: 2 
s2_dv1 ~~ s2_iv1 + s2_iv2 + s2_med1 + s2_med2 + s2_med3 + s2_med4 + s2_dv2
s2_dv2 ~~ s2_iv1 + s2_iv2 + s2_med1 + s2_med2 + s2_med3 + s2_med4
s2_iv1 ~~ s2_iv2 + s2_med1 + s2_med2 + s2_med3 + s2_med4
s2_iv2 ~~ s2_med1 + s2_med2 + s2_med3 + s2_med4
s2_med1 ~~ s2_med2 + s2_med3 + s2_med4
s2_med2 ~~ s2_med3 + s2_med4
s2_med3 ~~ s2_med4'

fit <- sem(multilevel.multigroup.regression.model.revised, data=df, cluster = "ID", estimator = "MLR", group = "Study") 

That model is giving me this error: 

Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;
  check your model and/or starting parameters in group 2.

I also tried running the same level 1 portions, but replicating the model at level 2, and I got the same error. The only thing I have been able to run without error is the same model above, but replacing both groups' level 2 models with just this one covariance between the dependent variables: 

for group 1: s1_dv1 ~~ s1_dv2
for group 2: s2_dv1 ~~ s2_dv2

When I do that, I get no error (just warning related to having no variance on a handful of clusters.

I'd be grateful for any advice about how I might remedy this error, or some other approach to doing what I'm trying to do. I'm ultimately wanting to compare the level 1 coefficients across groups, with something like this: 

lavTestWald(fit, constraints = c("a1==c1",
                                 "a2==c2",
                                 "a3==c3",
                                 "a4==c4",
                                 "a5==c5",
                                 "a6==c6"))
lavTestWald(fit, constraints = c("b1==d1",
                                 "b2==d2",
                                 "b3==d3",
                                 "b4==d4",
                                 "b5==d5",
                                 "b6==d6"))

All the best, 
Wayne
